observation.visible_scene: A deep-sea, dark blue underwater frame with a static white 'BBC' logo overlay in the top-left corner. The central subject is a long, thin, dark organism hanging diagonally from the upper-right toward the middle of the frame, its body studded with two parallel rows of tiny bright white dots (photophore-like specks). At the lower end of the body is a rounded head/bell structure with a side flap and a few brighter markings. The surrounding water is filled with scattered small cyan/green glowing streaks and blurry bokeh spots (suspended bioluminescent or reflective particles). The scene is dim, with a soft blue glow concentrated behind the organism.
visible_changes: The slender organism stays the persistent central subject throughout, keeping a roughly constant diagonal orientation from upper-right to center; its rows of white specks remain visible the whole time.

The head/bell at the lower end of the organism moves within the frame over the excerpt (drifting lower in the first half, then partly back up by the end), and its outline changes subtly from frame to frame, consistent with gentle undulation/contraction of the bell rather than the body translating away.

A localized green glow appears near the lower head around t≈1.0–1.2 s, and a separate bright green dot is visible on the body just above the head around t≈1.3–1.6 s, then fades; these read as transient bioluminescent flashes on/near the organism, not new objects.

The field of small cyan/green streaks and bokeh dots reconfigures continuously, shifting relative to the organism, indicating relative motion among the subject, the suspended particles, and the viewpoint.
The body's angle relative to the frame edges barely changes, so the dominant apparent motion is slow drift/tracking of the organism rather than a directed swim across the scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the green flashes originate from the organism's own bioluminescence or from passing particles is not established.
The cause of the apparent drift (current, the animal's movement, or camera motion) is unknown.
Events before t=0 and after t=3.2 s are not shown.
uncertain_details: Separating camera pan from organism motion is ambiguous because the background is dark and featureless.
The changing outline of the head/bell could be deformation, a viewpoint shift, or partial occlusion; the clip does not disambiguate.
The exact trajectory of the green dot on the body (traveling glow vs. particle passing in front) is not certain.
